reviews.text:
So as everyone knows about the supply problem everything is hard to get. With that being said we purchased a Carvin pool from Crown during the winter along with numerous upgrades including a pool heater. We waited until March 18th when the season opened and had the pool installed. We are totally happy with the sales and service but let me say this if you go the route we did there is a lot of expense that most are not aware of so do your research. The heater needed 220 volt which required a new panel cause we didn't have any room. it also required additional hard pluming to the heater. Again the staff is top notch but just be aware that one can spend a lot of money on above ground pools to have the paradise we all want in our back yards Thank you Crown for helping us with ours. I also want to say the installers were on point and did a great job.

Dave and Kat

I was in need of some pool equipment parts and came across Crown Pools on the internet.  It was getting near to closing time, so I called your Garland Road location and Marc answered the phone. A few days later, I was back in need of another part.  I was glad  to see Marc and I was on my way back home in a few minutes. reviews.text:
My wife and I purchased an 18' above ground pool from the Dallas location around 2 years ago. I can say that the customer service at both the Allen location and Dallas was amazing. They were excited to sell us a pool, and catered to us during the purchase.

Well, after we bought the pool things took a change. My wife and I had questions as would any first time pool owner. What chemicals do we use, how often, etc..

We would bring in routine water samples, either at Allen or Dallas. Everytime we did so, we would get a completely different set of chemicals to use in our mineral pool. Every time we spoke with an associate or manager, it was a different direction on what to put in our pool.

We were sold over $200 in pool chemicals, only to be told later, we were sold the wrong stuff. The manager apologized and said it's new staff that was hired. Ok, no problem, I've been a retail manager for 25+ years. I get it, but credit me and let me get the chemicals I should have gotten. Nope, no offer to take care of it. Just purchase the new chemicals. Absolutely ridiculous! The Allen location manager I spoke with made it good. She refunded the chemicals the Dallas location should have done to begin with.

Fast forward to this season, and I'm needing a new ionizer replacement cell for my mineral pool. Dallas location says in store to my wife and I that they are out of stock, but a female manager that was the would be bringing some to the store. Give them my name and number and they will call me when it's in... No phone call. I called to follow up and it's a short "no" we don't have it. No offer to help locate one or explain why I was never called.

I call Allen today, August 7th in the morning. A gentleman says he needs to ask his GM, and he promised he would call me back, being he knew Dallas never returned my call. Guess what? He never bothered to return my call.

All I'm trying to do is get the proper pool supplies from the supplier I purchased my pool from, and they don't seem to care at all about my wife and I, as customers.

It's always a different answer. Just go back and forth between the two stores and ask several employees and you'll get different answers every time. Why can't we just get a correct answer with what to use for our pool? Why is it after we purchased our pool, Crown doesn't seem to care at all?

It's beyond ridiculous that I have to go through this much trouble to spend money with this company.
When you as employees of Crown tell a customer you will call them back, do so! Two different Crown Pools in two days and nobody there can be bothered.

I found my Nature's Pure ionizer replacement cell online finally and ordered it there. Would like to have purchased it with Crown, unfortunately they couldn't be bothered.

John & Andrea C.
reviews.author: John Charles

data.summary: The reviews present a mixed but credible picture. The negative reviews on Yelp and Google are highly specific and consistent, detailing serious failures in communication, fulfillment, and post-sale service. The positive Google reviews are detailed but show a pattern of praising a specific contractor, suggesting the company's reputation may be heavily reliant on subcontractor performance. The significant rating discrepancy and specific complaint patterns indicate real operational problems, though not necessarily review fraud.
fake_signals: Multiple 5-star Google reviews specifically praise the same installer (Marcos Coronado) in similar language
Some 5-star reviews mention a dramatic turnaround in service from 'horrendous' to 'amazing', which could be incentivized
Low review volume on platforms like Yelp and Houzz relative to business age (54 years)
authentic_signals: Specific details in negative reviews (names, dates, amounts, specific problems like liner mix-up)
Varied writing styles and emotional authenticity across all reviews
Balanced 3-4 star reviews acknowledge both good service and external challenges (supply chain)
Long-term business history (54 years) suggests a mix of experiences over time
data.discrepancy_explanation: Significant discrepancy between Google (4.5) and Yelp (2.5) ratings. Yelp's low rating with 11 reviews suggests a pattern of negative experiences not fully reflected in the higher-volume Google reviews.
